items.topic: Current sign-up intake via WhatsApp group chat
items.statement: Current process: the referrer creates a WhatsApp group chat with the BA and the new sign-up; the BA sends a script asking for welcome-email screenshots, survey confirmation and the e-transfer email, in a fixed format (full name, ET email, casinos).
items.quote: Jay: I'll just share this uh Chrome uh tab here. So um you can see my screen in a second here. So this is uh we primarily use WhatsApp for uh most signups. Some people use iMessage. I just think uh WhatsApp is is better because iMessage limits you to only iPhone clients. So most people uh operate in and out of WhatsApp. All the BA chats are on WhatsApp and our sales chats are on WhatsApp. / So this is uh first step is send screenshots of welcome emails. The reason why we do this is if we don't get a screenshot of a welcome email, we can't confirm that that email is or is that sign up is actually new. / So full name, ET email, and what casinos they signed up for. / Jay: No, because the referer has to make the group chat.

items.statement: Current rule: sign-ups have 24 hours to return deposit/wager proof (transaction history); after a reminder, if there is no proof in 48 hours they are not considered for redeposits or other sites. Some reps take four or five days.
items.quote: after I I send off, I I like to tell them that they have 24 hours maximum to get me back the um the videos. Otherwise, like proof um and the proof is like uh transaction history in the casinos because we want to confirm that they actually met the casino requirement. So, they actually have to wager it. So, if they don't send it back in 24 hours, um I take note of it. I send them like another message just like reminding them. If I don't get it back in 48 hours, I don't consider them for like redeposits or any other sites. / If I don't get it back in 48 hours, I don't consider them for like redeposits or any other sites. / Jay: And yeah. Yeah. Like we we've encouraged multiple times like reps to implement 24-hour policy, / Jay: but there will be some people that take like four or five days sometimes.

items.statement: Very high-volume referrers (200-300 sign-ups a week) act as a proxy and forward sign-up details in an operations chat; Jay still requires a group chat with each sign-up for direct contact, but many do not do this.
items.quote: Those are the guys that are doing like 200 300 signups a week. They can't do this method because it would just be way too many group chats. So they have like um this would be called like for example uh Owen's operations chat. And if Owen was the referer, he would be the proxy here. / But I would tell them they still have to make a group chat with that one person. That way I can always have contact with them. Like let's say they run away or they don't do the the signups properly and the referer is not able to fix the problem, I'd want to contact them directly. So I I force people to always put me in a group chat with with their signups even if I never talk to them. / Jay: But uh a lot of people don't do that because it's just too many chats to manage.

Um, we kind of cuz the signups come at the most randomest hours of the day. Absolutely. Okay. Um the last question I'll ask and then we can move on from kind of the scams.

items.topic: More fraud controls in system to scale
items.statement: Ops mainly detects scams monthly through tracking reports. Joyce said that if they scale and add reps, the technology should have more controls and visibility over flagged players; Jay agreed. No specific control was defined.
items.quote: The only way we actually know if people are getting scammed, which is like 99% of the time, is when we actually look into the tracking numbers. So like if we're looking at OOLG reports, we're able to see exactly who deposited what and then identify who didn't deposit or who didn't track and see that they scammed us. Or maybe they didn't scam us, they just didn't go through the link. But that's kind of more so how we identify that now. And it's usually just throughout a month whenever we do tracking reports. / Joyce Kiddell: Got it. Okay. So I I do think like although you guys have done a great job of minimizing risk with our current workforce, it's like if we were to scale and bring on more reps, it's something that we should have more controls around within the technology. / Jay: Yeah, I I agree with that because I think the current reps are not getting scammed because of like Owen said experience and then on top of that a while ago we threatened to take their pay if they or cut their pay if they get scammed, right? because then their performance drops, pay drops. And so what we saw was people were paying a lot more attention when there was actually an incentive on the line. So or decent. So they started paying a lot more attention. So um we had like record low erosion numbers. Everything was good. Um, so like you said though, if yeah, if we bring on like a bunch more reps, then yeah, they need to unfortunately they they would have to in order to be at these guys level, they would have to get scammed a few times, but ideally we wouldn't want that want them to be scammed yet.
